source_artifacts.claim: Relevant earlier lessons and current level_38 placement in campaign order.
Current room defines the recoil trigger, lower support, unstable upper crossing, latching OPEN ISP pad, barriers, exits, and hint.
When both heroes support recoil tissue and exactly one leaves, the remaining hero launches upward.
Isp LOWER SUPPORT hold opens the Pac membrane and stabilizes the crossing; Pac OPEN ISP latch opens both barriers.
An unsupported unstable platform collapses after its configured occupied time, then resets.
Cana boomerang can dizzy Isp or shove Pac temporarily; this is interference, not damage.
Earlier recoil teaching explicitly describes stepping off tissue to launch the other hero and regrouping below after a miss.
Earlier room demonstrates an unstable crossing, hold/latch route pads, and pad stabilization.
Earlier Cana room introduces boomerang effect, including a Gem shove as an optional interaction.

prior_knowledge.concept: Both heroes stand on recoil tissue; when exactly one steps off, the remaining hero is launched. This room transfers that launch into a split route.

evidence.claim: level_37 precedes the current position.
Earlier subtitle and hint explicitly teach stepping off tissue to launch the partner.

prior_knowledge.concept: A hold pad can stabilize an unstable platform; a separate latching pad can open route barriers for the partner.

evidence.claim: level_36 precedes current room.
Earlier hint describes the safe landing and OPEN ISP role.
Earlier source defines hold stabilization and latching route unlock.

prior_knowledge.concept: Cana’s boomerang applies dizziness to Isp and shove to Pac, but it is not required for the demonstrated split route.

evidence.claim: level_41 precedes current level.
Earlier Cana room and hint establish the boomerang interaction.

mechanics.fact: The mandatory launch begins with both heroes supported by living_tissue. When exactly one leaves, recoil launches the remaining hero upward. The implied split is Isp stepping to the low support while Pac is launched toward the high crossing.

evidence.claim: Recoil is triggered by joint support followed by one hero leaving.
Both spawn on recoil tissue and upper crossing is unstable.
Villain dialogue says one goes up, one goes out; hint names Isp low and Pac high.
The ordinary route shows Isp moving right while Pac is airborne toward the upper route.

mechanics.fact: Isp holding LOWER SUPPORT stabilizes the upper crossing and opens Pac’s upper membrane. Pac reaches OPEN ISP on the crossing; its latch opens both the upper membrane and Isp lower gate, allowing the routes to reunite at the two lower exits.

evidence.claim: Pad effects and latching define the two route gates.
Hold pad effects stabilize; latching pad effects open configured doors.
At frame 323 Isp holds lower support while Pac occupies upper crossing; both pads and barriers are active.
Both heroes reach their matching exits after the split route.

mechanics.fact: The upper crossing collapses after 3.4 seconds if not stabilized and resets after 1.2 seconds; the fallback floor supports falls. Cana’s boomerang is automatically active but only adds temporary interference.

evidence.claim: Upper crossing collapse/reset timings and fallback floor.
Unstable platform timer and reset.
Cana boomerang has a repeating windup/cooldown and the room has no hazards.
Shove/dizzy are temporary movement effects.
Recorded route reaches both exits without deaths.

legal_routes.name: Isp holds the lower route while Pac crosses above and releases Isp

steps.action: Regroup both heroes on TISSUE so the recoil platform supports them at the same time.
steps.expected_feedback: Joint support primes the launch: when one hero steps off, the other springs upward.

evidence.claim: Both heroes start on living_tissue.
The launch requires joint support followed by one leaving.
Dialogue and hint cue the joint start.

steps.goal: Take the lower road and keep Pac’s upper crossing safe.
steps.action: Step off tissue to the right onto LOWER SUPPORT and remain there.
steps.expected_feedback: Isp holds the pad, which stabilizes upper_crossing and opens Pac’s upper membrane; Pac is launched upward from the tissue.

evidence.claim: LOWER SUPPORT is Isp-only and holds crossing stabilization.
At frame 323 Isp occupies lower support while Pac is on the crossing.

steps.goal: Use the launch to cross above, then release Isp.
steps.action: Steer left from the recoil launch onto upper_crossing and touch OPEN ISP at its left end.
steps.expected_feedback: The pad latches and opens the Isp lower gate; the one-off split paths can rejoin below for the exits.

evidence.claim: The upper route and its collapse/reset configuration.
OPEN ISP is Pac-only, latches and opens both gates.
At frame 323 Pac is on upper_crossing and OPEN ISP is latched.

steps.goal: Regroup at the matching exits after the split.
steps.action: Move right from the opened route; Isp follows the lower floor, while Pac leaves the high crossing and descends to the lower exit.
steps.expected_feedback: Both matching exits are reached; the elevated route is temporary traversal, not a separate high exit.

evidence.claim: Both exits are on the lower/right side of the room.
At frame 704 both heroes occupy their matching exits; route is complete.
Room subtitle and hint state the high/low split and regroup retry.
Ordinary-input main route completes in 704 frames with zero deaths.

isp: Steps from shared recoil tissue to Isp-only LOWER SUPPORT, stabilizing the crossing and opening Pac’s route while Pac crosses.
After Pac latches OPEN ISP, leaves support and reaches the lower Isp exit.
pac: Remains on recoil tissue when Isp leaves, launching onto the upper crossing.
Crosses to OPEN ISP and latches the gate for Isp, then descends/rejoins for the Pac exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Try to trigger the recoil launch before both heroes are standing on the tissue together.
common_mistakes.consequence: The recoil is conditional on joint support; if the pair never share support, stepping off will not launch the partner onto the upper crossing.
common_mistakes.recovery: Regroup both heroes on tissue and have Isp step off again; the fallback floor is safe.

evidence.claim: Joint support is required for launch.
Both start on tissue; fallback floor is beneath.

common_mistakes.mistake: Have Pac cross before Isp is holding LOWER SUPPORT, or let Isp leave the pad before Pac reaches OPEN ISP.
common_mistakes.consequence: The upper crossing is unstable and can collapse after 3.4 seconds without stabilization, dropping Pac to fallback floor and closing the hold-controlled Pac membrane.
common_mistakes.recovery: Keep Isp on LOWER SUPPORT until Pac latches OPEN ISP; if the crossing collapses, the hint says regroup below and retry after its 1.2 second reset.

evidence.claim: Collapse window and hold effect.
Collapse/reset behavior.
Hint explicitly says regroup below and try again.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assume the two exits are on different floors because the cue says one takes the high road and one the low road.
common_mistakes.consequence: The routes are split only during the puzzle: both matching exits are at the lower right, so Pac must eventually leave the upper crossing.
common_mistakes.recovery: After Pac activates OPEN ISP, descend/rejoin on the safe fallback floor and move to the Pac exit; Isp uses the opened lower gate.

evidence.claim: Both exits are positioned on the lower/right side.
Native trace completes both exits from their lower/right positions.

reasoning.rationale: The confirmed route has a linked sequence: both heroes share recoil tissue, Isp steps down to hold/stabilize the crossing, Pac is launched above and must press OPEN ISP, then the two paths reunite for exits. The visible high/low cue identifies the split but not the unusual recoil trigger or why Pac must release Isp.

evidence.claim: The step-off launch rule.
Lower hold and upper latch dependencies.
Trace shows the hero split with both route pads active.

cooperation.rationale: The heroes have distinct, reciprocal roles: Isp holds the lower support so Pac can cross high; Pac then latches OPEN ISP to release Isp. This is one meaningful handoff, not repeated simultaneous coordination. Both exits are lower/right after the split.

evidence.claim: Isp hold supports Pac; Pac latch opens Isp gate.
Both exits are lower/right.
Both actors occupy separate route roles at the handoff.

execution.rationale: Pac needs to steer a recoil launch horizontally onto the upper crossing, reach its far-left OPEN ISP pad, and later descend; Isp mainly steps right to the lower support and then exits. This is several controlled movements but not sustained precision for both heroes.

evidence.claim: Recoil and elevated crossing geometry.
The trace shows Pac on upper crossing and Isp at lower support.
Both later reach their exits.

timing.rationale: The 3.4-second crossing timer is a visible constraint unless Isp holds LOWER SUPPORT, which stabilizes it indefinitely for the crossing. This is a readable, repeatable setup window; the 1.2-second reset makes a missed crossing retryable.

evidence.claim: Crossing timer and hold stabilization.
Timer, collapse, and reset.
The route completes without death.

hazards.rationale: There are no authored hazards, and the full-width fallback floor catches falls from both tissue and the upper crossing. Boomerang effects are temporary interference rather than physical danger on this route.

evidence.claim: Fallback floor under recoil and crossing.
No hazards are authored.
Boomerang effects are temporary.
The ordinary route completes with zero deaths.

novelty.rationale: The recoil launch is taught at position 5 (level_37), and hold/latch stabilization for an unstable route is practiced at position 19 (level_36). This room joins those concepts into a high/low reciprocal route with exits that reunite below; it is a new combination, not a new mechanic.

evidence.claim: Earlier recoil and stabilization lessons precede this room.
Earlier recoil interaction.
Earlier hold/latch stabilization.
Current route combination.

recovery_cost.rationale: A failed launch or collapsed crossing drops onto the safe fallback floor. The hint directs players to regroup below; the crossing resets after 1.2 seconds, so the setup can be repeated without a long route reset.

evidence.claim: Safe floor and 1.2-second reset.
Hint says regroup and try again.
Unstable-platform retry behavior.

solution_clarity.rationale: The subtitle and visible pad cues say to split between low and high routes; the image marks the upper release pad and lower support. Which hero takes each role and why the step-off launches the partner still requires transfer from earlier recoil teaching. The labels also correctly signal that the split paths eventually reconnect at low exits.

evidence.claim: Subtitle says one hero takes each road and opening dialogue asks which way back.
The captured labels identify Pac opening Isp and Isp lower support; both exits are at the lower right.
The earlier lesson supplies the recoil step-off rule.

control_friction.rationale: Ordinary-input route feasibility does not establish two-human shared-keyboard reliability or contention. No direct two-human reliability evidence is available.

confidence_reason: The source explicitly defines recoil, stabilization, latch, timer, and safe-floor behavior; the ordinary-input trace reaches both exits. The route cues are visible, while novice interpretation and two-human input reliability remain unmeasured.

confirmed: The visible subtitle and route labels cue a low/high split, and the boomerang produces different temporary effects for Isp and Pac.
The room requires a sequence that opens one route for the other hero before both matching exits can be reached.
missed_mechanics: This room’s central transfer is recoil: when both heroes share tissue and exactly one steps off, the other springs upward. The relevant earlier lesson is level_37, not boomerang room level_25.
Isp’s LOWER SUPPORT is a hold pad that stabilizes the unstable upper crossing; Pac’s OPEN ISP is a platform-mounted latch that releases Isp through the lower gate.
The high/low paths are temporary split routes; both matching exits are at the lower/right edge, so the heroes regroup after the handoff.
The boomerang is not a required control choice in the demonstrated route; it is a repeated temporary interference.
incorrect_inferences: The first-pass prior ledger attributed the boomerang effect lesson to level_25; the actual earlier campaign source is level_41.
The first-pass reading that the exits themselves are at different heights was mistaken: the visible exits are both lower/right; the high/low cue names the traversal paths.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises 2 to 3 because the source/trace establish a multi-link recoil launch, held stabilization, release latch, and route reunion rather than an unspecified assignment between two paths.
Cooperation remains 2: source confirms one reciprocal handoff (Isp supports Pac’s crossing, then Pac releases Isp), without repeated or simultaneous coordination.
Execution remains 2: the route requires one steered launch and traverse for Pac, but Isp’s lower support and both final floor exits are comparatively simple.
Timing changes from unknown to 2 because upper_crossing collapses after 3.4 seconds unless Isp holds the stabilizing pad; its reset is 1.2 seconds and the hold creates a safe repeatable window.
Hazards changes from unknown to 0 because the fallback floor under the entire room catches falls; no authored lethal hazards exist.
Novelty remains 2 but its causal basis changes: recoil was taught at level_37 and hold/latch stabilization at level_36; the split-and-rejoin route recombines those prior lessons.
Recovery changes from unknown to 1 because the source hint explicitly tells players to regroup below and retry, and the crossing reset is short.
Clarity remains 2: labels cue the split and who opens which gate, while the recoil transfer still depends on prior lesson and the exit height must be read separately from route height.
unresolved: Whether players transfer level_37’s recoil launch to this level without a hint is not measured by the idle captures or scripted route.
Whether Cana’s recurring boomerang distracts or disrupts first-time play is not established by the one successful route trace; it does not create a lethal hazard in source.
The first-pass idle RECOVER/DIZZY animation does not establish an input-driven mistake or player recovery; it is not treated as witnessed feedback.
Two-human keyboard reliability is unmeasured, so control friction remains null.

single_operator_note: One operator would need to coordinate Isp’s hold on LOWER SUPPORT with Pac’s launch, upper crossing, and OPEN ISP latch, then switch attention to both exit movements. That switching demand is separate from the two-human baseline score.
